# rgflux

> Rare event kinetics over rgsaddle and rgmin.

The Rust API separates rate estimators and trajectory sampling from
potential energy surfaces and molecular dynamics engines.

## Complete documentation

## rgflux

`rgflux` separates rare-event kinetics from specific force fields and molecular dynamics codes. Every sampler drives the `DynamicsEngine` trait, while recorded trajectory estimators such as `kappa::bennett_chandler` stay engine-free.

   :maxdepth: 1
   :caption: Guides

## Getting started

## Install

Add `rgflux` from crates.io (alongside `ndarray` and `rgsaddle` when defining custom potential surfaces) cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025`:

```console
$ cargo add rgflux
```

Enable optional `rgpot`, `rgpot-session`, and `lammpc` features as needed:

```console
$ cargo add rgflux --features rgpot
$ cargo add rgflux --features rgpot-session
$ cargo add rgflux --features lammpc
```

The `lammpc` feature links `liblammpc` from `LAMMPC_LIB_DIR`, from `pkg-config` when available, or from `LAMMPC_DIR` (install prefix with `lib/` or `lib64/` and `include/`) when `pkg-config` is not configured. Its build also needs the `capnp` command-line tool on `PATH`; the `rgpot` and `rgpot-session` features do not.

## 1. Engine-free Bennett-Chandler recrossing

`kappa::bennett_chandler::estimate_bennett_chandler` estimates the time-dependent transmission coefficient \(\kappa(t)\) and its stationary plateau mean with a block-averaged standard error from `stats` cite:`bennettMolecularDynamics1977,chandlerStatisticalMechanics1978,flegalMcmcThirdSignificantFigure2008` directly from recorded dividing-surface velocity and side histories:

```rust
use rgflux::kappa::bennett_chandler::{
    BennettChandlerConfig, ReactiveTrajectory, Side, estimate_bennett_chandler,
};

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let trajectories = vec![
        ReactiveTrajectory::new(1.2, vec![Side::Product; 16])?,
        ReactiveTrajectory::new(-0.9, vec![Side::Reactant; 16])?,
        ReactiveTrajectory::new(0.8, vec![Side::Product; 16])?,
    ];
    let estimate = estimate_bennett_chandler(&trajectories, &BennettChandlerConfig::default())?;
    assert_eq!(estimate.plateau, 1.0);
    assert_eq!(estimate.standard_error, 0.0);
    assert!(estimate.stationarity.is_stationary);
    Ok(())
}
```

## 2. Drive a surface with `NativeEngine` and evaluate an OH-TST rate

Implement `rgsaddle::PointSurface` (returning potential energy \(V(\mathbf{x})\) and gradient \(+\nabla V(\mathbf{x})\)), construct `engine::native::NativeEngine`, and call `ohtst::optimize_hyperplane` cite:`johannessonOptimizationHyperplanar2001,vineyardFrequencyFactors1957` to place the dividing hyperplane at the barrier top and evaluate the harmonic hyperplanar TST rate:

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{DynamicsEngine, HyperplaneConstraint, ThermostatConfig};
use rgflux::ohtst::{OhtstConfig, optimize_hyperplane};

struct QuarticDoubleWell1D;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for QuarticDoubleWell1D {
    fn eval(&self, x: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let u = x[0];
        let well = u * u - 1.0;
        Ok((0.25 * well * well, Array1::from_vec(vec![u * well])))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let cfg = NativeConfig::default()
        .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0]))
        .with_thermostat(
            ThermostatConfig::default()
                .with_gamma(1.0)
                .with_temperature(0.1),
        )
        .with_seed(17);
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(QuarticDoubleWell1D, cfg)?;
    engine.set_positions(Array1::from_vec(vec![-1.0]).view())?;

    let seed_plane =
        HyperplaneConstraint::from_direction(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0]).view(), 0.0)?;
    let ohtst_cfg = OhtstConfig::default()
        .with_burn_in_steps(64)
        .with_min_sample_steps(128)
        .with_sample_step_factor(4)
        .with_seed(17);
    let estimate = optimize_hyperplane(&mut engine, &seed_plane, &ohtst_cfg)?;

    assert_eq!(estimate.plane.offset, 0.0);
    assert!(estimate.rate > 0.0 && estimate.standard_error.is_finite());
    Ok(())
}
```

## How-to guides

## Sample holonomic hyperplane mean forces and configurations

Construct a `HyperplaneConstraint` from a direction vector and scalar offset \(c\), configure `HyperplaneConfig`, and call `hyperplane::sample_hyperplane` over any `DynamicsEngine` cite:`sprikFreeEnergyConstrained1998,leimkuhlerGeodesicIntegration2016`. `sample_hyperplane` installs the constraint, runs BAOAB + RATTLE equilibration and production steps, estimates \(\langle \lambda \rangle = dA/dc\) with a block-averaged standard error, retains dividing-surface configurations every `retention_stride` steps, and restores the engine's initial positions, velocities, periodic cell, thermostat, and constraint before returning:

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{DynamicsEngine, HyperplaneConstraint, ThermostatConfig};
use rgflux::hyperplane::{HyperplaneConfig, sample_hyperplane};

struct DoubleWell2D;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for DoubleWell2D {
    fn eval(&self, r: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let (x, y) = (r[0], r[1]);
        let well = x * x - 1.0;
        Ok((
            0.25 * well * well + 0.5 * y * y,
            Array1::from_vec(vec![x * well, y]),
        ))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(
        DoubleWell2D,
        NativeConfig::default()
            .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 1.0]))
            .with_thermostat(
                ThermostatConfig::default()
                    .with_gamma(1.0)
                    .with_temperature(0.2),
            )
            .with_seed(11),
    )?;
    engine.set_positions(Array1::from_vec(vec![-0.3, 0.0]).view())?;

    let plane =
        HyperplaneConstraint::from_direction(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 0.0]).view(), -0.3)?;
    let cfg = HyperplaneConfig::default()
        .with_burn_in_steps(100)
        .with_sample_steps(400)
        .with_retention_stride(20)
        .with_time_step(0.01)
        .with_seed(11);

    let sample = sample_hyperplane(&mut engine, &plane, &cfg)?;
    assert!(sample.mean_force.is_finite());
    assert!(sample.standard_error >= 0.0);
    assert_eq!(sample.configurations.dim(), (20, 2));
    assert!(engine.constraint().is_none());
    Ok(())
}
```

## Diagnose correlated samples with batch means, effective sample size, and Geweke windows

Use `stats::batch_means` for the mean and its correlation-aware standard
error, `stats::effective_sample_size` for the Geyer initial monotone sequence
estimate, and `stats::check_stationarity` before accepting an equilibrium or
plateau window
cite:`goswamiBayesianHierarchical2025,flyvbjergErrorEstimates1989,geyerPracticalMcmc1992,gewekeEvaluatingAccuracy1992,flegalMcmcThirdSignificantFigure2008`.

For \(a\) non-overlapping batches of width \(b\), batch means \(Y_j\), and
\(n = ab\) retained observations, the asymptotic variance and standard error
are

\[
 \widehat{\sigma}_{\mathrm{BM}}^2 =
 \frac{b}{a - 1}\sum_{j=1}^{a}(Y_j-\bar{Y})^2,\qquad
 \operatorname{SE}(\bar{X}) =
 \sqrt{\widehat{\sigma}_{\mathrm{BM}}^2/n}.
\]

Geyer's paired initial positive and monotone autocovariance sequence gives the
statistical inefficiency \(g = 2\tau_{\mathrm{int}}\) and
\(n_{\mathrm{eff}} = n/g\). The Geweke diagnostic compares leading and
trailing windows with

\[
 \lvert z\rvert =
 \frac{|\bar{X}_{\mathrm{first}}-\bar{X}_{\mathrm{last}}|}
 {\sqrt{\operatorname{SE}_{\mathrm{first}}^2+
        \operatorname{SE}_{\mathrm{last}}^2}}.
\]

```rust
use rgflux::stats::{
    StatsConfig, batch_means, check_stationarity, effective_sample_size,
};

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let samples: Vec<f64> = (0..256)
        .map(|i| {
            let phase = (i % 16) as f64;
            (phase * std::f64::consts::TAU / 16.0).sin()
        })
        .collect();
    let config = StatsConfig::default()
        .with_min_batches(8)
        .with_stationarity_first_fraction(0.25)
        .with_stationarity_last_fraction(0.50)
        .with_max_z_score(3.0);

    let estimate = batch_means(&samples, &config)?;
    let n_eff = effective_sample_size(&samples)?;
    let stationarity = check_stationarity(&samples, &config)?;

    assert!(estimate.standard_error >= 0.0);
    assert_eq!(estimate.n_eff, n_eff);
    assert!(n_eff >= 1.0 && n_eff <= samples.len() as f64);
    assert!(stationarity.is_stationary);
    Ok(())
}
```

## Assemble a rate-network edge and kMC configuration

A directed rate network stores non-negative first-order rates \(k_{ij}\).
Its continuous-time master equation is

\[
 \frac{dp_i}{dt} =
 \sum_{j\ne i} p_j k_{ji} -
 p_i\sum_{j\ne i}k_{ij}.
\]
For a BKL or Gillespie residence-time step in state \(i\), define
\(K_i = \sum_j k_{ij}\), select event \(j\) with probability
\(k_{ij}/K_i\), and draw
\(\Delta t = -\ln u/K_i\) for \(u\) uniform on \((0,1)\)
cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,goswamiConcurrencyAkmc2025,bortzNewAlgorithmMonteCarlo1975,gillespieGeneralMethod1976,henkelmanLongTimeScale2001`.

`RateEdge::new` validates one directed edge. `NetworkConfig` records thermal
and detailed-balance policy, while `RateTableConfig` records trajectory
limits. `build_rate_table` is deliberately a typed migration boundary in this
release and returns `FluxError::Unimplemented` rather than silently producing
an incomplete table.

```rust
use rgflux::FluxError;
use rgflux::network::{
    NetworkConfig, RateEdge, RateTableConfig, build_rate_table,
};

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let edges = vec![
        RateEdge::new(0, 1, 2.0)?,
        RateEdge::new(1, 0, 0.5)?,
    ];
    let network = NetworkConfig::default()
        .with_temperature(500.0)
        .with_boltzmann(1.0)
        .with_enforce_detailed_balance(true)
        .with_min_rate(1.0e-12);
    let trajectory = RateTableConfig::default()
        .with_max_steps(10_000)
        .with_seed(7);

    assert_eq!(trajectory.max_steps, 10_000);
    assert!(matches!(
        build_rate_table(2, &edges, &network),
        Err(FluxError::Unimplemented(_))
    ));
    Ok(())
}
```

## Place a fixed-normal OH-TST dividing hyperplane and evaluate the rate

Pass a seed `HyperplaneConstraint` and `OhtstConfig` to `ohtst::optimize_hyperplane` cite:`goswamiAdaptivePruning2026,johannessonOptimizationHyperplanar2001,bligaardOptimizationHyperplanar2005,vineyardFrequencyFactors1957`. Even when the seed offset is displaced from the saddle (here \(c_0 = -0.4\) while the barrier sits at \(c^\ddagger = 0\)), `optimize_hyperplane` relaxes into the reactant minimum, brackets and bisects the stationary dividing hyperplane along the seed normal, samples the curvature probe plane, and returns \(k_{\mathrm{OHTST}} = \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\kappa / \mu}\exp(-\Delta V / k_{\mathrm{B}}T)\) (with \(\mu\) from `rgsaddle::flux_mass`) alongside its delta-method standard error:

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{DynamicsEngine, HyperplaneConstraint, ThermostatConfig};
use rgflux::ohtst::{OhtstConfig, optimize_hyperplane};

struct ObliqueDoubleWell2D;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for ObliqueDoubleWell2D {
    fn eval(&self, r: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let u = 0.6 * r[0] + 0.8 * r[1];
        let v = -0.8 * r[0] + 0.6 * r[1];
        let well = u * u - 1.0;
        let du = u * well;
        let dv = 2.0 * v;
        Ok((
            0.25 * well * well + v * v,
            Array1::from_vec(vec![0.6 * du - 0.8 * dv, 0.8 * du + 0.6 * dv]),
        ))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(
        ObliqueDoubleWell2D,
        NativeConfig::default()
            .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![2.0, 8.0]))
            .with_thermostat(
                ThermostatConfig::default()
                    .with_gamma(1.0)
                    .with_temperature(0.1),
            )
            .with_seed(33),
    )?;
    engine.set_positions(Array1::from_vec(vec![-0.6, -0.8]).view())?;

    // Seed normal (3, 4) / 5 = (0.6, 0.8) with a displaced offset c_0 = -0.4.
    let seed_plane =
        HyperplaneConstraint::from_direction(Array1::from_vec(vec![3.0, 4.0]).view(), -0.4)?;
    let cfg = OhtstConfig::default()
        .with_max_outer_steps(16)
        .with_max_translation(0.25)
        .with_burn_in_steps(64)
        .with_min_sample_steps(128)
        .with_sample_step_factor(8)
        .with_time_step(0.01)
        .with_seed(33);

    let est = optimize_hyperplane(&mut engine, &seed_plane, &cfg)?;
    assert!(est.plane.offset.abs() < 1e-12);
    assert!(est.rate > 0.0 && est.standard_error.is_finite());
    Ok(())
}
```

## Compute a transition rate with direct Forward Flux Sampling (FFS)

Initialize the engine inside reactant basin \(A\) (\(\lambda(\mathbf{x}_0) \le \lambda_0\)) with positive Langevin friction \(\gamma > 0\), specify strictly increasing interfaces \(\lambda_0 < \lambda_1 < \dots < \lambda_n\) in `FfsConfig`, and pass an order-parameter closure \(\lambda(\mathbf{x})\) to `ffs::forward_flux_rate` cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,allenSamplingRareSwitching2005,allenSimulatingRareEvents2006,allenForwardFluxEfficiency2006,allenForwardFluxReview2009`:

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{DynamicsEngine, ThermostatConfig};
use rgflux::ffs::{FfsConfig, forward_flux_rate};

struct QuarticDoubleWell1D;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for QuarticDoubleWell1D {
    fn eval(&self, x: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let dx = x[0] * x[0] - 1.0;
        Ok((dx * dx, Array1::from_vec(vec![4.0 * x[0] * dx])))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let cfg = NativeConfig::default()
        .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0]))
        .with_thermostat(
            ThermostatConfig::default()
                .with_gamma(2.0)
                .with_temperature(0.9),
        )
        .with_seed(11);
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(QuarticDoubleWell1D, cfg)?;
    engine.set_positions(Array1::from_vec(vec![-1.0]).view())?;
    engine.shoot_velocities(11)?;

    let ffs_cfg = FfsConfig::default()
        .with_interfaces(vec![-0.8, -0.4, -0.1, 0.2])
        .with_points_per_interface(16)
        .with_trials_per_interface(64)
        .with_max_trial_steps(3_000)
        .with_max_flux_steps(400_000)
        .with_burn_in_steps(50)
        .with_time_step(0.01)
        .with_seed(11);

    let est = forward_flux_rate(&mut engine, |x| x[0], &ffs_cfg)?;
    assert!(est.initial_flux > 0.0);
    assert_eq!(est.interface_probabilities.len(), 3);
    assert!(est.rate > 0.0 && est.standard_error > 0.0);
    assert_eq!(engine.positions()[0], -1.0);
    Ok(())
}
```

## Compute a free-energy profile, barrier and rate along a reaction path (PAFI workflow)

Projected Average Force Integration (PAFI) cite:`goswamiEnhancedClimbingImage2026,goswamiReproducibleOrchestration2026,swinburneUnsupervisedCalculation2018` takes the images of a converged minimum-energy path, for example from a nudged elastic band, and returns the free-energy profile \(F(s)\), the barrier \(\Delta F\), the dividing plane, and the normalized rate \(k\) through `pafi::pafi_profile`. The method is described under /Projected Average Force Integration/ in the explanation page and the defaults in the reference page.

The example runs a straight path from the minimum \(x = -1\) to the saddle \(x = 0\) of the widening double well \(V(x, y) = (1 - x^2)^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}(1.5 + 0.5x)y^2\) at \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T = 0.2\), where the exact barrier is \(\Delta F = 1 + \tfrac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T \ln 1.5\). It uses 33 planes. The free-energy profile is the cubic Hermite integral of the plane means, so the trapezoid bias of about \(0.0156\,(8/(\text{planes} - 1))^2\) (0.025 with the default 9 planes, 0.0016 with 33) is the scale of the zero-temperature guard and is not left in \(\Delta F\). The run checks the barrier within five standard errors.

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, Array2, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::engine::ThermostatConfig;
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::pafi::{PafiConfig, pafi_profile};
use rgflux::stats::StatsConfig;

struct WideningWell2D;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for WideningWell2D {
    fn eval(&self, r: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let (x, y) = (r[0], r[1]);
        let well = 1.0 - x * x;
        let k = 1.5 + 0.5 * x;
        Ok((
            well * well + 0.5 * k * y * y,
            Array1::from_vec(vec![-4.0 * x * well + 0.25 * y * y, k * y]),
        ))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let temperature = 0.2;
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(
        WideningWell2D,
        NativeConfig::default()
            .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 1.0]))
            .with_thermostat(
                ThermostatConfig::default()
                    .with_gamma(1.5)
                    .with_temperature(temperature),
            )
            .with_seed(19),
    )?;

    // PAFI samples at `config.planes` planes along a spline through these
    // images. Two images would do for a straight path; a curved path needs
    // the images of the converged band.
    let config = PafiConfig::default()
        .with_planes(33)
        .with_burn_in_steps(500)
        .with_sample_steps(8_000)
        .with_stats(StatsConfig::default().with_min_batches(4))
        .with_seed(19);
    let images = 5;
    let mut path = Array2::<f64>::zeros((images, 2));
    for k in 0..images {
        path[[k, 0]] = -1.0 + (k as f64) / ((images - 1) as f64);
    }

    let profile = pafi_profile(&mut engine, path.view(), &config)?;
    assert_eq!(profile.arc_lengths.len(), config.planes);
    assert_eq!(profile.free_energy[0], 0.0);
    assert_eq!(profile.dividing_index, config.planes - 1);

    let analytic = 1.0 + 0.5 * temperature * 1.5_f64.ln();
    assert!(profile.barrier_error > 0.0);
    assert!((profile.barrier - analytic).abs() < 5.0 * profile.barrier_error);
    assert!(profile.normalized_rate > 0.0 && profile.normalized_rate_error > 0.0);
    Ok(())
}
```

Points to adapt for a real path:

- *Images*: `path_images` has one row per image and one column per degree of freedom, in the units and ordering of the engine. The planes are placed by the spline, not at the images, so the number of images and `planes` are independent.
- *Planes and tolerance*: The zero-temperature check compares \(\lvert I_T - \Delta E_0\rvert / \max(E_{\mathrm{unit}}, \lvert\Delta E_0\rvert)\) with a dimensionless tolerance. Here \(I_T\) is the trapezoid integral of \(dV/ds\), \(\Delta E_0\) is the endpoint energy change and \(E_{\mathrm{unit}}\) is one energy unit of the engine. The stored default is about 2.6% for 9 planes. While the field retains that value, the effective tolerance scales as \((\text{planes} - 1)^{-2}\) when `planes` changes. A value supplied with `with_zero_temperature_tol` is used unchanged. A sharper path can require a larger explicit tolerance. A failing check returns `FluxError::InvalidConfig` before any sampling.
- *Statistical error*: Set `with_target_error(0.01)` and `with_max_rounds(8)` to repeat sampling in rounds of `sample_steps` until `barrier_error` reaches the target. Reaching `max_rounds` first is not an error, so compare `barrier_error` with the target yourself.
- *Reproducibility*: The seed of plane \(k\) in round \(r\) is `seed + 4099 * k + 1000003 * r`, so a fixed `with_seed` gives the same profile for a deterministic engine.
- *Engine*: `pafi_profile_dyn` accepts `&mut dyn DynamicsEngine`. The engine is restored on return, with the stochastic stream the only exception.

## Shoot Bennett-Chandler reactive-flux trajectories and compare with Kramers

Combine `hyperplane::sample_hyperplane` (to harvest thermalized configurations on the dividing surface \(x = 0\)) with `kappa::bennett_chandler::shoot_bennett_chandler` and compare the resulting plateau transmission coefficient against `kappa::kramers_transmission_coefficient` cite:`goswamiEfficientExploration2025,bennettMolecularDynamics1977,chandlerStatisticalMechanics1978,kramersBrownianMotion1940`:

```rust
use ndarray::{Array1, ArrayView1};
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{HyperplaneConstraint, ThermostatConfig};
use rgflux::hyperplane::{HyperplaneConfig, sample_hyperplane};
use rgflux::kappa::bennett_chandler::{ShootingConfig, shoot_bennett_chandler};
use rgflux::kappa::kramers_transmission_coefficient;

struct SeparableDoubleWell2D;

impl rgsaddle::PointSurface for SeparableDoubleWell2D {
    fn eval(&self, r: ArrayView1<f64>) -> Result<(f64, Array1<f64>), rgsaddle::SaddleError> {
        let (x, y) = (r[0], r[1]);
        let dx = x * x - 1.0;
        Ok((dx * dx + y * y, Array1::from_vec(vec![4.0 * x * dx, 2.0 * y])))
    }
}

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let gamma = 6.0;
    let omega_b = 2.0;
    let kramers = kramers_transmission_coefficient(gamma, omega_b)?;

    let dividing_surface =
        HyperplaneConstraint::new(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 0.0]), 0.0)?;
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(
        SeparableDoubleWell2D,
        NativeConfig::default()
            .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 1.0]))
            .with_thermostat(
                ThermostatConfig::default()
                    .with_gamma(gamma)
                    .with_temperature(0.08),
            )
            .with_seed(42),
    )?;

    let surface_sample = sample_hyperplane(
        &mut engine,
        &dividing_surface,
        &HyperplaneConfig::default()
            .with_burn_in_steps(100)
            .with_sample_steps(400)
            .with_retention_stride(10)
            .with_time_step(0.02)
            .with_seed(42),
    )?;

    let shoot_cfg = ShootingConfig::default()
        .with_steps(120)
        .with_time_step(0.05)
        .with_antithetic(true)
        .with_seed(99);
    let bc = shoot_bennett_chandler(
        &mut engine,
        &dividing_surface,
        surface_sample.configurations.view(),
        &shoot_cfg,
    )?;

    assert!(bc.plateau > 0.0 && bc.standard_error > 0.0);
    assert!(kramers > 0.3 && kramers < 0.31);
    Ok(())
}
```

## Wrap an `rgmin` objective with `EindirSurface`

Any `eindir_core::DifferentiableObjective<f64>` (such as `rgmin::Oracle`) can be adapted into a `ForceSurface` via `engine::EindirSurface` and passed to `NativeEngine`:

```rust
use ndarray::Array1;
use rgflux::engine::native::{NativeConfig, NativeEngine};
use rgflux::engine::{DynamicsEngine, EindirSurface};

fn main() -> Result<(), rgflux::FluxError> {
    let oracle = rgmin::Oracle::unbounded(2, |x| {
        let energy = 0.5 * (x[0] * x[0] + 4.0 * x[1] * x[1]);
        let grad = Array1::from_vec(vec![x[0], 4.0 * x[1]]);
        (energy, grad)
    });
    let surface = EindirSurface::new(oracle);
    let mut engine = NativeEngine::new(
        surface,
        NativeConfig::default()
            .with_masses(Array1::from_vec(vec![1.0, 2.0]))
            .with_seed(7),
    )?;
    engine.shoot_velocities(7)?;
    let report = engine.step(0.01)?;
    assert!(report.potential_energy.is_finite() && report.kinetic_energy.is_finite());
    Ok(())
}
```

## Reference

## Module overview

| Module | Scope | Status |
|---+---+---|
| `engine` | `DynamicsEngine` trait, `ForceSurface`, `EindirSurface`, `HyperplaneConstraint`, `ThermostatConfig`, `SurfaceVelocityPolicy`, `StepReport`, `native` BAOAB/RATTLE backend, optional direct `lammpc` backend, `rgpot` static PES wrapper, and `rgpot-session` MD session skeleton (`openmm`, `nblib`, `lammps`) | Implemented (`native`, `lammpc`, `rgpot`) and `rgpot-session` skeleton |
| `stats` | Batch means, effective sample size `n_eff`, and stationarity diagnostics | Implemented; spline-propagated profile covariance helpers are not yet implemented |
| `kappa::bennett_chandler` | Engine-free reactive-flux estimator and `DynamicsEngine` trajectory shooter | Implemented |
| `kappa` | Kramers analytical barrier-recrossing factor; surface-shooting quench classifiers and first-crossing estimators | `kramers_transmission_coefficient` and `KappaConfig` implemented; the quench and first-crossing drivers are not yet implemented |
| `hyperplane` | Constrained hyperplane sampling (`sample_hyperplane`) and zero-variance control variates | Mean constraint force and configuration retention implemented; the in-plane virial, torque, and control variates are not yet implemented |
| `pafi` | Projected Average Force Integration along reaction paths (`PafiConfig`, `FreeEnergyProfile`, `pafi_profile`, `pafi_profile_dyn`) | Implemented: mass-metric spline planes with not-a-knot ends, zero-temperature trapezoid path-force check, burn-in and batch-means sampling per plane, adaptive rounds to a target error, cubic Hermite free-energy profile, global interpolant maximum, projected-frequency reactant partition, barrier, and normalized rate with propagated errors; the engine is restored on return |
| `ohtst` | OH-TST with a fixed hyperplane normal (`optimize_hyperplane`) | Implemented for a fixed normal with `rgsaddle::flux_mass`; normal optimization is not yet implemented |
| `ffs` | Forward Flux Sampling across ordered interfaces (`forward_flux_rate`) | Implemented: flux collection, staged trials, and uncertainty propagation. Exit restores positions, velocities, the periodic cell, the thermostat, and the constraint; the stochastic stream is left where the run put it |
| `network` | Symmetry-resolved rate networks and kinetic Monte Carlo rate tables (`NetworkConfig`, `RateTableConfig`, `RateEdge`, `build_rate_table`) | `RateEdge::new` and configuration types implemented; `build_rate_table` is not yet implemented |
| `error` | Shared `FluxError` enum and `From<rgsaddle::SaddleError>` conversion | Implemented |
| `config` | Internal `with_setters!` macro used by public configuration types | Private module, so it has no importable public path; every generated public setter is listed in the inventory below |

## Configuration structs and field defaults

Every public configuration struct is `#[non_exhaustive]` and provides chainable `#[must_use]` `with_*` builder methods. Setter methods for `Option<T>` fields accept `impl Into<Option<T>>` so passing a bare `T` sets `Some(T)` and passing `None` clears the option.

### `engine::ThermostatConfig`

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `gamma` | `f64` | `1.0` | Langevin friction coefficient \(\gamma \ge 0\) in inverse time units (`0.0` selects velocity-Verlet NVE) |
| `temperature` | `f64` | `1.0` | Absolute temperature \(T \ge 0\) |
| `boltzmann` | `f64` | `1.0` | Boltzmann constant \(k_{\mathrm{B}} > 0\) in the engine's energy-per-temperature unit |

Method: `ThermostatConfig::thermal_energy(&self) -> Result<f64, FluxError>` validates finiteness and domain bounds and returns \(k_{\mathrm{B}} T\).

### `engine::HyperplaneConstraint`

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `normal` | `Array1<f64>` | `vec![1.0]` | Unit Euclidean normal \(\mathbf{n}\) (\(\lvert\lVert\mathbf{n}\rVert_2 - 1\rvert \le \text{UNIT\_NORMAL\_TOL}\)) oriented from reactant to product |
| `offset` | `f64` | `0.0` | Scalar offset \(c\) in \(\sigma(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{n} \cdot \mathbf{x} - c = 0\) |

Constructors and methods: `HyperplaneConstraint::new(normal, offset)`, `from_direction(direction, offset)`, `validate(&self)`, and `signed_distance(&self, positions)`.

### `engine::native::NativeConfig`

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `masses` | `Array1<f64>` | `vec![1.0]` | Strictly positive per-coordinate masses \(m_i > 0\) (sets `dof = masses.len()`) |
| `thermostat` | `ThermostatConfig` | `ThermostatConfig::default()` | Langevin thermostat parameters |
| `constraint` | `Option<HyperplaneConstraint>` | `None` | Optional active holonomic hyperplane constraint |
| `projection` | `ConstraintProjection` | `ConstraintProjection::Rattle` | Holonomic constraint projection scheme (`Rattle` or `Shake`) |
| `cell` | `Option<[f64; 9]>` | `None` | Optional row-major \(3 \times 3\) periodic simulation box |
| `seed` | `u64` | `1` | Initial deterministic PRNG seed for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck thermal noise |

### `engine::lammpc::LammpcConfig` (feature `lammpc`)

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `atomic_numbers` | `Vec<i32>` | `vec![18, 18]` | Non-empty atomic numbers in live atom order (\(N_{\mathrm{atoms}}\) entries; `dof = 3 * N_atoms`) |
| `type_to_atomic_number` | `Vec<i32>` | `vec![18]` | Non-empty LAMMPS type map (\(\text{type } i+1 \mapsto Z\)) |
| `masses_by_type` | `Vec<f64>` | `vec![39.948]` | Strictly positive per-type masses in amu (length must match `type_to_atomic_number`) |
| `pair_style` | `String` | `"lj/cut 8.5"` | Non-empty LAMMPS `pair_style` specification |
| `pair_coeffs` | `Vec<String>` | `vec!["1 1 0.010323 3.405"]` | LAMMPS `pair_coeff` argument strings |
| `extra_setup` | `Vec<String>` | `vec![]` | Optional additional LAMMPS setup lines applied after pair setup |
| `boundary` | `String` | `"p p p"` | LAMMPS boundary specification string |
| `suffix` | `String` | `""` | Optional LAMMPS accelerator suffix (`omp`, `gpu`, `kk`) |
| `thermostat` | `ThermostatConfig` | `ThermostatConfig::default()` | Langevin thermostat in metal units (\(\gamma\) in \(\mathrm{ps}^{-1}\), \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) in eV) |
| `constraint` | `Option<HyperplaneConstraint>` | `None` | Optional holonomic hyperplane constraint |
| `cell` | `Option<[f64; 9]>` | `Some(diag(30.0, 30.0, 30.0))` | Optional row-major \(3 \times 3\) simulation cell in Å |
| `seed` | `u64` | `1` | Initial deterministic PRNG seed passed to `lammpc_session_md_initialize` |

### `engine::rgpot::RgpotConfig` (feature `rgpot`)

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `atomic_numbers` | `Vec<i32>` | `vec![1]` | Non-empty atomic numbers \(Z_i\) (\(N_{\mathrm{atoms}}\) entries; `dof = 3 * N_atoms`) |

### `ohtst::OhtstConfig`

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `max_outer_steps` | `usize` | `32` | Maximum bracketing / outer steps (\(\ge 1\)); reactant minimization budget is \(8 \times \text{max\_outer\_steps}\) |
| `patience` | `usize` | `3` | Consecutive accepted planes within gradient noise (reserved for variational normal optimization) |
| `max_translation` | `f64` | `0.25` | Step size for dividing-surface bracketing and upper cap on curvature probe distance \(\delta\) (\(> 0\)) |
| `max_rotation` | `f64` | `0.25` | Trust-region cap on normal rotation angle in radians (\(\ge 0\)) |
| `min_overlap` | `f64` | `0.03` | Minimum two-state BAR overlap before warning (reserved for variational normal optimization) |
| `use_mbar` | `bool` | `true` | Combine reversible work across plane nodes with MBAR (reserved for variational normal optimization) |
| `seed` | `u64` | `1` | Deterministic PRNG seed forwarded to curvature sampling |
| `stats` | `StatsConfig` | `StatsConfig::default()` | Batch-means settings for the curvature probe sample |
| `burn_in_steps` | `usize` | `256` | Equilibration steps discarded before the curvature probe sample |
| `min_sample_steps` | `usize` | `128` | Lower bound on curvature-sample steps (\(\ge 2\)) |
| `sample_step_factor` | `usize` | `64` | Multiplier on `max_outer_steps` for curvature-sample length (\(\max(\text{max\_outer\_steps} \times \text{sample\_step\_factor}, \text{min\_sample\_steps})\)) |
| `retention_stride` | `usize` | `16` | Steps between retained configurations in the curvature sample (\(\ge 1\)) |
| `time_step` | `f64` | `0.01` | Integration timestep \(\Delta t > 0\) for the curvature sample |

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `interfaces` | `Vec<f64>` | `vec![-0.5, 0.0, 0.5]` | Strictly increasing order-parameter levels \(\lambda_0 < \lambda_1 < \dots < \lambda_n\) (\(\text{len} \ge 2\)) |
| `points_per_interface` | `usize` | `128` | Crossing configurations \(M_0\) collected at \(\lambda_0\) (\(\ge 2\)) |
| `trials_per_interface` | `usize` | `256` | Trial trajectories \(K\) launched at each stage (\(\ge 1\)) |
| `max_trial_steps` | `usize` | `10_000` | Maximum integration steps per trial before aborting (\(\ge 1\)) |
| `max_flux_steps` | `usize` | `200_000` | Maximum integration steps during initial flux collection (\(\ge 1\)) |
| `burn_in_steps` | `usize` | `0` | Burn-in steps discarded before counting \(\lambda_0\) crossings |
| `time_step` | `f64` | `0.005` | Integration timestep \(\Delta t > 0\) |
| `seed` | `u64` | `1` | Deterministic PRNG seed |
| `stats` | `StatsConfig` | `StatsConfig::default()` | Batch-means controls for the inter-crossing intervals |

### `pafi::PafiConfig`

| Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---+---+---+---|
| `planes` | `usize` | `9` | Number of hyperplanes at equal spacing along the spline path (\(\ge 2\)) |
| `burn_in_steps` | `usize` | `500` | Equilibration steps discarded on each hyperplane before sampling (\(\ge 1\)); every plane and round restarts from the anchor |
| `sample_steps` | `usize` | `4_000` | Production steps added per hyperplane and round (\(\ge 2\)) |
| `time_step` | `f64` | `0.002` | Integration timestep \(\Delta t > 0\) in engine time units |
| `target_error` | `Option<f64>` | `None` | Optional target standard error on \(\Delta F\) (finite, \(\ge 0\)); `None` runs one round |
| `max_rounds` | `usize` | `4` | Maximum sampling rounds (\(\ge 1\)); later rounds run only while `target_error` is set and not reached, and missing it is not an error |
| `zero_temperature_tol` | `f64` | \(2 (\pi^2 / 12) / 8^2 \approx 0.0257\) | Dimensionless tolerance for \(\lvert I_T - \Delta E_0\rvert / \max(E_{\mathrm{unit}}, \lvert\Delta E_0\rvert)\), where both energies use engine energy units and \(E_{\mathrm{unit}}\) is one such unit (finite, \(\ge 0\)); see the scaling note below |
| `seed` | `u64` | `1` | Base of the per-plane seeds `seed + 4099 * plane + 1000003 * round` (wrapping) |
| `stats` | `StatsConfig` | `StatsConfig::default()` | Batch-means settings for the per-plane force series |

Here \(I_T\) is the trapezoid integral of \(dV/ds\) over the plane anchors and \(\Delta E_0\) is the endpoint energy change. The ratio is relative to \(\lvert\Delta E_0\rvert\) at or above one engine energy unit and bounds the absolute discrepancy below that scale.

The value stored by `PafiConfig::default()` is the 9-plane value shown in the table. While the field retains that value, the effective tolerance is \(2 (\pi^2 / 12) / (\text{planes} - 1)^2\), so changing `planes` scales the tolerance with the trapezoid error. An explicitly different value is used unchanged. The scaling follows a quarter-turn circular arc through a harmonic well. A path that turns further can need a larger explicit tolerance.

### `pafi::FreeEnergyProfile`

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---+---+---|
| `arc_lengths` | `Vec<f64>` | Plane coordinates \(s_k\): the mass-weighted chord-length parameter of the spline, from 0 at the first image to the total path length at the last, at equal spacing. Not scaled to \([0, 1]\) |
| `free_energy` | `Vec<f64>` | \(F(s_k) - F(s_0)\) by cubic Hermite quadrature of the plane means; the first entry is 0. With two planes the derivative correction cancels and the rule is the trapezoid rule. With three planes it is exact for a quadratic gradient. With four or more planes it is exact for a cubic gradient |
| `standard_error` | `Vec<f64>` | Standard error of `free_energy`: batch-means plane-force error through the Hermite weights, combined by hypot with the absolute Hermite-minus-trapezoid difference on the same nodes; the first entry is 0 |
| `barrier` | `f64` | \(\Delta F\), the global maximum of the Hermite interpolant, which can exceed every sampled value |
| `barrier_error` | `f64` | Standard error of `barrier`: the same combination at `s*` |
| `dividing_index` | `usize` | First plane with the highest sampled free energy. The interpolant maximum recorded in `dividing_arc` can lie on a different interval |
| `dividing_arc` | `f64` | Arc length \(s^*\) of the global maximum of the Hermite interpolant |
| `reactant_frequency` | `f64` | \(\omega_0 = ( \mathbf{n}^\top \mathbf{H}^{-1} \mathbf{n} )^{-1/2}\) from the mass-weighted Hessian at the first image, in inverse engine time |
| `reactant_partition` | `f64` | \(Z_R = \sqrt{2\pi k_{\mathrm{B}}T} / \omega_0\), in units of \(s\) |
| `reactant_log_partition` | `f64` | \(\ln Z_R = \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(2\pi k_{\mathrm{B}}T) - \ln \omega_0\) |
| `normalized_rate` | `f64` | \(k = (\omega_0 / 2\pi) \exp(-\Delta F / k_{\mathrm{B}}T)\) in inverse engine time |
| `normalized_log_rate` | `f64` | \(\ln k = \ln \omega_0 - \ln(2\pi) - \Delta F / k_{\mathrm{B}}T\), finite when the exponential in `normalized_rate` underflows |
| `normalized_rate_error` | `f64` | Delta-method standard error \(k\,\sigma_{\Delta F} / k_{\mathrm{B}}T\). \(Z_R\) is a property of the reactant Hessian, so its sampling sensitivity is zero |
| `quadrature_residual` | `f64` | Largest absolute gap between the Hermite integral of \(dV/ds\) and the endpoint energy change. The acceptance check remains the trapezoid comparison in `PafiConfig::zero_temperature_tol` |

### `network::NetworkConfig` and `RateTableConfig`

| Struct | Field | Type | Default | Constraint / Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NetworkConfig` | `temperature` | `f64` | `300.0` | Absolute temperature \(T > 0\) |
| `NetworkConfig` | `boltzmann` | `f64` | `1.0` | Boltzmann constant \(k_{\mathrm{B}} > 0\) |
| `NetworkConfig` | `enforce_detailed_balance` | `bool` | `true` | Enforce detailed balance across reverse edges |
| `NetworkConfig` | `min_rate` | `Option<f64>` | `None` | Optional rate floor below which negligible channels are pruned |
| `RateTableConfig` | `max_steps` | `usize` | `100_000` | Maximum kMC steps per trajectory (\(\ge 1\)) |
| `RateTableConfig` | `seed` | `u64` | `1` | Deterministic PRNG seed for event selection and residence-time draws |

## Public output types, functions, and constants

| Item | Signature / Fields | Description |
|---+---+---|
| `engine::UNIT_NORMAL_TOL` | `64.0 * f64::EPSILON` | Unit Euclidean normal tolerance (\(2^{-46}\)) |
| `engine::HYPERPLANE_PROJECTION_TOL` | `16.0 * f64::EPSILON` | Relative holonomic SHAKE residual tolerance (\(2^{-48}\)) |
| `engine::DEFAULT_REJECTION_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `4_096` | Default maximum redraw attempts in `SurfaceVelocityPolicy::RejectRedraw` |
| `engine::lammpc::MASS_VELOCITY_TO_EV` | `0.000_103_642_696_562_621_75` | LAMMPS metal-unit factor `mvv2e` converting \(\mathrm{amu} \cdot (\text{Å/ps})^2\) to eV |
| `engine::draw_maxwell_boltzmann_velocities` | `(masses, kbt, seed) -> Result<Array1<f64>, FluxError>` | Deterministic Box-Muller draw \(v_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, k_{\mathrm{B}}T / m_i)\) |
| `engine::reflect_velocity_in_place` | `(&mut velocities, masses, normal) -> Result<f64, FluxError>` | Kinetic-energy-preserving mass-weighted Householder reflection across `normal` |
| `stats::SERIES_FLAT_TOL` | `64.0 * f64::EPSILON` | Relative flatness tolerance for constant-series detection |
| `stats::VARIANCE_REL_FLOOR` | `SERIES_FLAT_TOL * SERIES_FLAT_TOL` | Relative variance floor (\(2^{-92}\)) |
| `stats::MIN_STATIONARITY_SAMPLES` | `4` | Minimum window length for `check_stationarity` |
| `stats::BatchEstimate` | `mean`, `standard_error`, `variance`, `batch_count`, `batch_size`, `n_samples`, `n_eff`, `tau_int` | Output of `stats::batch_means(samples, config)` |
| `stats::StationarityReport` | `is_stationary`, `z_score`, `max_z_score`, `drift_slope`, `first_mean`, `second_mean` | Output of `stats::check_stationarity(samples, config)` |
| `stats::effective_sample_size` | `(samples) -> Result<f64, FluxError>` | Geyer initial-monotone-sequence effective sample size \(n_{\mathrm{eff}}\) |
| `kappa::kramers_transmission_coefficient` | `(gamma, barrier_frequency) -> Result<f64, FluxError>` | Kramers spatial-diffusion factor \(\kappa_{\mathrm{K}} = \sqrt{1 + \alpha^2} - \alpha\) |
| `kappa::bennett_chandler::BennettChandlerEstimate` | `kappa_t`, `plateau`, `standard_error`, `n_eff`, `plateau_window`, `stationarity`, `positive_flux_count` | Output of `estimate_bennett_chandler` and `shoot_bennett_chandler` |
| `hyperplane::HyperplaneSample` | `plane`, `mean_force`, `standard_error`, `configurations` | Output of `hyperplane::sample_hyperplane(engine, plane, config)` |
| `ohtst::OhtstEstimate` | `plane`, `rate`, `standard_error` | Output of `ohtst::optimize_hyperplane(engine, seed_plane, config)` |
| `ffs::FfsEstimate` | `initial_flux`, `interface_probabilities`, `rate`, `standard_error` | Output of `ffs::forward_flux_rate(engine, order_param, config)` |
| `pafi::FreeEnergyProfile` | `arc_lengths`, `free_energy`, `standard_error`, `barrier`, `barrier_error`, `dividing_index`, `dividing_arc`, `reactant_frequency`, `reactant_partition`, `reactant_log_partition`, `normalized_rate`, `normalized_log_rate`, `normalized_rate_error`, `quadrature_residual` | Output of `pafi::pafi_profile(engine, path_images, config)` and `pafi::pafi_profile_dyn(engine, path_images, config)`; see the field table in the configuration section |
| `network::RateEdge` | `from`, `to`, `rate` (`RateEdge::new(from, to, rate)`) | Directed elementary transition edge in `network::build_rate_table` |

### Estimator and sampling entry points

| Item | Inputs | Result and reference |
|---+---+---|
| `stats::batch_means` | Sample slice and `StatsConfig` | `BatchEstimate`; equations and runnable example in `howto.org` |
| `stats::effective_sample_size` | Sample slice | Geyer \(n_{\mathrm{eff}}\); equations and runnable example in `howto.org` |
| `stats::check_stationarity` | Sample slice and `StatsConfig` | `StationarityReport`; Geweke equation and runnable example in `howto.org` |
| `hyperplane::sample_hyperplane` | Mutable engine, plane, and `HyperplaneConfig` | `HyperplaneSample`; constrained mean-force guide in `howto.org` |
| `ohtst::optimize_hyperplane` | Mutable engine, seed plane, and `OhtstConfig` | `OhtstEstimate`; harmonic rate guide in `howto.org` |
| `ffs::forward_flux_rate` | Mutable engine, order parameter, and `FfsConfig` | `FfsEstimate`; direct FFS guide in `howto.org` |
| `pafi::pafi_profile` | Mutable engine, path image matrix, and `PafiConfig` | `FreeEnergyProfile`; PAFI guide in `howto.org` |
| `pafi::pafi_profile_dyn` | Mutable `dyn DynamicsEngine`, path image matrix, and `PafiConfig` | Trait-object form of `pafi_profile` with identical estimator and restoration semantics |
| `kappa::estimate_bennett_chandler` | Recorded `ReactiveTrajectory` slice and `BennettChandlerConfig` | `BennettChandlerEstimate`; reactive-flux equation in `howto.org` |
| `kappa::shoot_reactive_trajectories` | Mutable engine, dividing surface, initial positions, and `ShootingConfig` | Validated trajectory records used by the Bennett-Chandler estimator |
| `kappa::shoot_bennett_chandler` | Mutable engine, dividing surface, initial positions, and `ShootingConfig` | Shoots trajectories and returns `BennettChandlerEstimate`; runnable guide in `howto.org` |
| `kappa::kramers_transmission_coefficient` | Friction \(\gamma\) and barrier frequency \(\omega_b\) | Analytical Kramers factor; equation and comparison in `howto.org` |
| `network::build_rate_table` | State count, `RateEdge` slice, and `NetworkConfig` | Typed `FluxError::Unimplemented` migration boundary; master-equation and kMC guide in `howto.org` |

### Engine trait and concrete methods

Every concrete engine implements the same `DynamicsEngine` contract. The
method paths for each implementation are retained in the generated inventory,
while this table defines their shared semantics.

| Method | Contract |
|---+---|
| `dof` | Return the scalar coordinate count |
| `masses` | Borrow one strictly positive mass per coordinate |
| `positions`, `velocities` | Borrow current unwrapped coordinates or Cartesian velocities |
| `set_positions`, `set_velocities` | Validate shape and finiteness, overwrite state, and project onto an active constraint |
| `cell`, `set_cell` | Read, install, or clear the row-major \(3 \times 3\) periodic cell |
| `thermostat`, `set_thermostat` | Read or validate and install `ThermostatConfig` |
| `constraint`, `set_constraint` | Read, install, or clear `HyperplaneConstraint` |
| `energy_and_forces` | Return \(V(\mathbf{x})\) and physical force \(-\nabla V(\mathbf{x})\) |
| `kinetic_energy` | Return \(\tfrac12\sum_i m_i v_i^2\) |
| `step` | Advance by a finite positive timestep and return `StepReport` |
| `reseed` | Replace the engine stochastic stream |
| `shoot_velocities` | Draw Maxwell-Boltzmann velocities from a deterministic seed |
| `reflect_velocity` | Apply the mass-metric Householder reflection and return \(\mathbf{n}\cdot\mathbf{v}\) |
| `apply_dividing_surface` | Enforce positive normal velocity with `SurfaceVelocityPolicy` |

`ForceSurface::energy_and_forces` is the static-surface counterpart. The
blanket `PointSurface` implementation negates the supplied gradient.
`EindirSurface::new` wraps a differentiable objective and `inner` borrows it.
`StepReport::new` constructs the three end-of-step diagnostics.

| Concrete inherent API | Meaning |
|---+---|
| `NativeEngine::new` | Build the pure Rust engine at the projected origin with zero velocity |
| `NativeEngine::surface` | Borrow its `ForceSurface` |
| `NativeEngine::projection` | Read the active `Rattle` or `Shake` algorithm |
| `NativeEngine::reseed_rng`, `NativeEngine::reseed` | Reset its Langevin stream |
| `RgpotSurface::new`, `RgpotSurface::n_atoms` | Build the optional static callback surface and read its atom count |
| `SessionEngineKind::engine_name` | Return `openmm`, `nblib`, or `lammps` |
| `RgpotSessionEngine::new`, `engine_kind`, `rgpot_version_major` | Build and inspect the optional session adapter |
| `LammpcEngine::new` | Build the direct optional `liblammpc` session engine |

### Bennett-Chandler support types

`Side::from_signed_distance` maps a positive signed coordinate to `Product`
and all other values to `Reactant`. `Side::indicator` returns one or zero for
those states. `ReactiveTrajectory::new` validates finite initial normal
velocity and a non-empty side history. Its public fields are
`initial_normal_velocity` and `sides`. The complete `BennettChandlerEstimate`
field set is listed above.

## Error variants (`FluxError`)

| Variant | Payload | Trigger condition |
|---+---+---|
| `EmptyInput` | `&'static str` | Empty sample slice, trajectory list, mass vector, or direction vector |
| `NoPositiveFlux` | unit | No reactive-flux trajectory has `initial_normal_velocity > 0` |
| `NonStationaryPlateau` | `z_score`, `max_z_score`, `drift_slope` | Candidate Bennett-Chandler plateau window exceeds `max_z_score` |
| `Shape` | `expected`, `got`, `context` | Coordinate, velocity, normal, mass, or trajectory length mismatch |
| `NonFinite` | `&'static str` | `NaN` or infinite input, energy, force, rate, or intermediate value |
| `InvalidConfig` | `&'static str` | Configuration parameter or physical invariant out of domain |
| `ConstraintViolation` | `residual`, `tolerance` | Relative hyperplane residual after SHAKE projection exceeds `HYPERPLANE_PROJECTION_TOL` |
| `SurfaceRejection` | `max_attempts` | `SurfaceVelocityPolicy::RejectRedraw` exhausted `max_attempts` |
| `Surface` | `String` | Potential energy surface callback failure or converted `rgsaddle::SaddleError` |
| `BackendUnavailable` | `&'static str` | Unlinked external MD session call on `RgpotSessionEngine` or unsupported unconstrained Langevin / constrained NVE mode in `LammpcEngine` |
| `Lammpc` | `String` | Error returned by the `lammpc_session_*` C ABI or Cap'n Proto message decoding |
| `Unimplemented` | `&'static str` | Entry point that is not yet implemented (`build_rate_table`) |

## Binding surface

### C ABI

`rgflux` exports no `extern "C"` function and has no C header in this release.
The optional `lammpc` engine consumes, but does not re-export, the following
`liblammpc` C ABI symbols:

| Purpose | Consumed symbols |
|---+---|
| Session lifecycle | `lammpc_session_create_from_config`, `lammpc_session_destroy`, `lammpc_abi_version` |
| Force evaluation | `lammpc_session_calculate_result`, `lammpc_potential_result_size_for_force_input` |
| Constrained dynamics | `lammpc_session_md_initialize`, `lammpc_session_md_step`, `lammpc_session_md_set_velocities`, `lammpc_session_md_state` |
| Unconstrained NVE dynamics | `lammpc_session_nve_set_positions`, `lammpc_session_nve_set_velocities`, `lammpc_session_nve_step`, `lammpc_session_nve_state` |
| Errors and capabilities | `lammpc_last_error`, `lammpc_capabilities_result` |

All declarations are private implementation details in
`src/engine/lammpc.rs`. The public Rust boundary is `LammpcConfig`,
`LammpcEngine`, and the `DynamicsEngine` implementation listed below.

The `rgpot` feature consumes `rgpot_core::potential::PotentialImpl` through
the external `rgpot_force_input_t` and `rgpot_force_out_t` callback contract.
The `rgpot-session` feature targets the external `rgpot_md_session_*` session
contract for creation, state transfer, force evaluation, reseeding, and
Langevin stepping. These symbols are not declared or exported by `rgflux`.
Unavailable session calls return `FluxError::BackendUnavailable`, while direct
`liblammpc` failures return `FluxError::Lammpc`.

### Python

`rgflux` has no Python extension module, Python package, or type stub in this
release. Python callers need a separate downstream wrapper. Consequently
there are no Python names beyond the Rust inventory below.

## Public API documentation coverage

The release audit uses `cargo-public-api` with every feature enabled. It
counts modules, types, variants, fields, constants, functions, trait methods,
inherent methods, builder methods, and public re-export paths. Generated
trait implementations and blanket implementations are omitted because they
do not add an `rgflux` declaration.

Before this audit, 0 of 563 qualified public item paths had an explicit
qualified entry in the Org reference. The gaps were primarily builder methods,
`DynamicsEngine` methods on concrete engines, optional engine methods,
constants, enum variants, and public re-export paths. After this audit, the
generated inventory below maps all 563 of 563 paths to this page. The
descriptive tables above document semantics, defaults, constraints, outputs,
and errors. The how-to page documents every estimator workflow with runnable
Rust, equations, and literature citations.

The generated block is authoritative. Run
`python3 scripts/generate_api_inventory.py` after changing public Rust API.
